children: After consolidating over the previous seven to eight sessions, the market resumed its upward momentum on Friday, with the Nifty 50 rising 286 points despite weakness across global markets.
The benchmark index extended the rally that began on Thursday, signalling a renewed improvement in investor sentiment.
Among Nifty constituents, Apollo Hospitals and Axis Bank were the top performers, while Titan Company and Tata Steel were among the key laggards.

Sectoral buying broadened during the session, with the Nifty IT index recovering after several sessions of underperformance. FMCG and Metal were among the few sectoral indices to end marginally lower.

Banking stocks led the market rally through the week, with the Nifty Bank index gaining 5.9% on a week-on-week basis. PSU banks continued to outperform, while private sector banks also witnessed strong buying interest.
The broader market performance was mixed. The Nifty Midcap 100 advanced 0.66%, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 declined 0.13%, indicating relatively stronger buying interest in mid-cap stocks.

Looking ahead, market participants expect the gradual uptrend to continue, supported by strong foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows, improving earnings visibility and a firmer rupee. FIIs have reportedly invested ₹1,01,641 crore in November, marking their highest monthly net purchases since November 2020. The rupee has also strengthened to 92.6 against the US dollar, its strongest level in seven months.
On the domestic front, investors will track the November monthly futures and options (F&O) expiry scheduled for Monday.

Globally, the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation reading and the second estimate of US third-quarter GDP, both due on Wednesday, will be key data points. Flash purchasing managers' index (PMI) readings for November are also on the watchlist earlier in the week.
Nagaraj Shetti of HDFC Securities said the Nifty has decisively moved above the key resistance level of 25,500 and is now advancing towards its previous record highs.

According to Shetti, the benchmark's underlying trend remains firmly positive. Having cleared the 25,500 hurdle, the index could move towards 26,000 and subsequently 26,350 over the next one to two weeks.
He added that any consolidation or decline could find support around 25,500, as the earlier resistance level has now turned into support.
Osho Krishan of Angel One said the 26,000 mark is the next immediate milestone for the Nifty. If the current momentum continues, the index could also retest its previous all-time high of 26,373.
On the downside, the 25,500-25,450 range has emerged as a strong support zone, supported by significant put writing. This could help absorb any intermittent profit-taking, he said.

Vatsal Bhuva of LKP Securities said 26,000 would be the immediate resistance, while 25,500 remains a crucial support level. He sees the Nifty moving towards 26,500 and believes a buy-on-dips approach should remain the preferred strategy.

The Bank Nifty extended its record-setting run, scaling a fresh all-time high for the second consecutive session and ending 2.49% higher, close to the day's high. The banking index has gained nearly 8,000 points over the past 12 trading sessions.

Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities identified the 64,000-64,100 range as the immediate support zone for the Bank Nifty. A decisive break below this level could trigger short-term profit-taking, potentially dragging the index towards 63,600.
On the upside, the 65,000-65,100 range is the immediate resistance zone. Significant call writing at these levels could limit further gains in the near term, Shah said.

title: Nifty Outlook for November 23: Can index cross 26,000 and move towards 26,500 in the week ahead?
